clue.text: A cold flagstone cracked in summer residence

indicators.note: something cracked is broken up, so the letters of the preceding phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cold paving slab has split at someone's holiday home.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal palace in the Alban Hills outside Rome is where the Pope traditionally spends the summer months.

definitions.meaning: flicking rapidly between television stations with the remote control
a booze cruise is a quick ferry trip across the English Channel to buy cheap drink in France, so one is hopping over the water

explanation.surface: Someone flicking the TV remote while on a cheap drinks trip abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: A booze cruise is a British day trip by ferry to France to stock up on cheaper alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic: surfing through TV stations is called this, and literally it describes crossing the stretch of sea between England and France.

clue.text: The French discretely invested in bullion libraries — any one of four, or 21

definitions.text: The French discretely invested in bullion libraries — any one of four, or 21

parts.words: The French discretely invested in bullion libraries — any one of four, or 21
parts.note: put the French article la into bullion libraries as two separate letters, an L and an A, and the phrase splits into bull, lion, libra and aries: four star signs, each one an example of the answer, as is a star (21)

explanation.surface: An instruction about French money being sunk into gold-bullion archives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discretely' means separately: the L and the A of 'la' go in at different places, making BULL LION and LIBRA ARIES. The answer is defined by example, by any of those four, or by 21 across, STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus (the bull), Leo (the lion), Libra and Aries are each one of the twelve astrological star signs.

clue.text: Card player, West, losing first holding ace

indicators.note: the shortened word wraps around and holds the next piece
the word West drops its opening letter

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A bridge player sitting West loses the opening trick despite holding an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass point, so 'West' looks like part of the definition but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In contract bridge the four seats are named by compass point, and each seat's occupant is a player in that position.

indicators.note: cut means the final letter of the word for bars is chopped off

parts.note: a grating is a framework of parallel bars

explanation.surface: Bars have reduced their pastry or pie crust portions.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratin is the browned crust of breadcrumbs or cheese on top of a dish.

clue.text: Fastidiousness having links with NHS body

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun for fine points of fussy detail, matched loosely by this abstract noun

parts.note: NICE is the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, which advises the UK's National Health Service
ties are links or bonds

explanation.surface: An NHS regulator is accused of fussiness because of its connections.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service. 'with' places the body's name beside the links, ahead of them in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fussy precision over small details shows itself in attention to fine points and subtleties of etiquette.

definitions.meaning: members of a fraternal friendly society founded in eighteenth-century England

explanation.definitionFit: Split 3,7 it means strange chaps; as one word it names the members of the Independent Order, a benevolent fraternal society.

parts.note: to fall on something is to set about it eagerly, as on food
Hard Times is a novel by Charles Dickens

explanation.surface: Starting an exciting book eagerly, only to find it is an ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon a period of poverty or misfortune is to undergo hardship.

parts.note: getting ready to travel means filling luggage, and on a swimming break the swimwear goes in too

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means get ready to leave, and trunks are both large luggage cases and men's swimming shorts.

definitions.meaning: the golf course in Georgia that hosts the Masters tournament
Lady Bracknell, aunt of Algernon in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, has this first name

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a golf course belongs to someone's aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Algernon Moncrieff's aunt in The Importance of Being Earnest is Lady Augusta Bracknell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Augusta National club's course and Lady Bracknell's Christian name share the same word.

indicators.note: returns means the whole string, everything on top of the date, is read backwards

parts.note: all means everything
1 is the Roman numeral I and 12 is the twelfth month, December, abbreviated DEC

explanation.surface: A grade sends everything back on the first of December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ALLIDEC (ALL, then I DEC for the first of December, written 1/12 in British style) round.
explanation.definitionFit: A diacritic, the hook placed under a letter c to show it is pronounced soft, as in façade.

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Asking what number, and guessing roughly a dozen.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock in the daytime is midday.

clue.text: State capital's poor supply of candy

definitions.meaning: rock is a stick of hard seaside sweet, so a meagre supply is not much of it

explanation.surface: A state capital is said to be short of sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock is the hard stick candy sold at British seaside resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arkansas capital's name read literally is a small amount of rock, the hard sugary confection.

clue.text: Traps Burmese possibly taking naughty touches

parts.note: a Burmese is a breed of cat, so this is a definition by example

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving, so the letters of touches are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Burmese cat sets traps and makes cheeky pats at things.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap someone into a mistake or reveal their wrongdoing is to expose them; also a cricket dismissal by a catch.

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase All the are taken and rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A dramatic pronouncement that every letter in the post is crushing news.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deadly or destructive enough to kill is ruinous, devastating in effect.

clue.text: Preface to comment on past health?

definitions.meaning: a phrase used to open a remark, as in 'So, what now?'
a comment that one was healthy at that time

explanation.surface: An introduction to remarks about someone's medical history.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a conversational opener, and literally says someone was in good health at that earlier time.

definitions.meaning: Troy is the city of the Iliad's story

explanation.surface: Asking about the wisdom of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 4,4, the answer reads SAGA CITY, a description of Troy, setting of Homer's epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen judgement and wisdom are the qualities of a sage, hence shrewd insight.

parts.note: a gardener's term for fertiliser spread on the soil surface, here read as the outermost layer of clothes

explanation.definitionFit: A heavy coat is worn over everything else, so it is the clothing on top.

definitions.meaning: bladed weapons are cutters; the apostrophe stands for the plural
one of the four suits of the tarot pack, alongside cups, wands and coins

explanation.surface: Describing the outfit worn by a tailor's cutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blades for cutting and slashing are weapons; the same word names a tarot suit.

clue.text: Book in which cure includes tips of rue and burdock

indicators.note: includes means the word for cure takes the selected letters inside it

parts.note: to heal is to cure

indicators.note: tips of means the first letters of the two plant names

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy book whose cure contains bits of rue and burdock.
explanation.definitionFit: A book describing plants and their medicinal properties is a traditional herbal.

clue.text: One out walking in the buff — lover of last night?

definitions.meaning: a person strolling along the seafront for pleasure
a fan of the Proms who goes to the Last Night of the Proms concert

explanation.surface: Someone walking naked outdoors, who was someone's lover the night before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the buff' looks like nudity; buff is a fan. The Proms are a London summer concert season ending with the patriotic Last Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means someone taking a leisurely stroll, and also a concertgoer at the Proms.

indicators.note: tailed means the surname loses its final letter, as a tail is cut off

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer

explanation.surface: A top drummer was followed.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means principal or outstanding, as a lead performer is.

indicators.note: dropped means the last letter falls away from the garment's name

parts.note: a tanga is a style of bikini bottom or briefs

explanation.surface: A bikini bottom falls off and someone gets slapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smack' looks like a slap but means a taste, as in a smack of garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a distinct flavour or trace, as in a smack of salt.

clue.text: Capital! Top flier going tail first

indicators.note: the final letter of the combined pieces moves to the front

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the letter I for the one
a robin is a bird, a flier

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at a first-rate bird flying backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like the old exclamation of approval, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Kenya.

indicators.note: embracing means the superhero's name wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: the Penguin is a villain whose enemy is the caped crusader of Gotham
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero hugs an everyday oarsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rows or hires out small boats is called this.

clue.text: They know their place, we hear

definitions.text: They know their place, we hear

parts.words: They know their place, we hear
parts.note: place said aloud is plaice, a flatfish, so these are fish experts

explanation.definitionFit: Zoologists who study fish would know the flatfish plaice, which is pronounced like place.
